newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Aug gains more after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Aug gains more after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderate session, with August holding a modest gain on hot weather and firmer cash prices, then moving up more after bullish inventory data.

August closed up 1.2 cents at $2.174 per million British thermal units, then climbed to $2.194 on ACCESS after the AGA weekly stock report. September settled 0.2 cent higher at $2.158. Other deferreds ended narrowly mixed.
"It's (the AGA number) slightly bullish, but it's not enough to move the market too far either way," said one Midwest trader.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 87 bcf, the low end of average expectations in the 85-95 bcf range. Overall stocks are still 215 bcf, or 14 percent, over year ago.

Eastern inventories increased by 65 bcf and remained 76 bcf, or nine percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage gained six bcf last week but continued to lag 1996 levels by about seven percent. Stocks in the producing region were still 47 percent above last year.

Despite the scorching heat wave this week that saw power demand jump to record levels in parts of the Midwest and East, traders said more seasonal forecasts later this week and next helped temper the bulls.
And chart traders said the sharp decline this week in August open interest indicated the recent rally was mostly short covering, not new buying.

Despite the short-term uptrend, most agreed it would take an August close above major resistance along the down trendline at $2.23 to turn the picture decidedly bullish. Support was seen in the $2.15 area and then at last week's low of $2.051.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast gas firmed a couple of cents to about $2.20. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly at $2.10-13. New York city gate gas also gained a couple of cents to the mid-to-high $2.50s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip was unchanged at $2.223. NYMEX said 31,364 contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 34,795.
On the KCBT, August finished two cents higher at $2.08, while deferreds ended up by one-half to one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 9.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
